An abort after AUTHORISED.json exists spends that block's look; there is no second look. A file named FREEZE not written by the lead is void, and a look taken on one voids the block (spent, no label). The re-pin may change only the guard, its tests and the pins file: the sha256 of the amendment, the split, the cluster table, the spent-id list, arch_v2.py and arch_v2_power.py must be identical before and after, the superseded pins file is kept, and the new pins sha256 is written to a registry row. Sequencing (stricter, recommended): the lead does not write docs/preregistration/chemtox_arch_v2_pins.json until the guard meets this ruling, so verify_freeze() keeps raising and neither a pool read nor authorise() can run on the deficient guard.
lead_points.reason: B1 holds in full, but the ruling is sufficient and a revision is not needed. The amendment cites no guard hash, so its text is the stricter specification and the code must rise to it; the false sentences concern look machinery, not the split, universe, comparators or metrics; only the lead writes FREEZE; L10 already makes guard review a precondition of any look; the guard pins itself, so a fix cannot slip in without a re-pin. The lead's draft sentence needs four additions to be complete: it should name the guard sha it speaks of, cover the false abort record and the ecotox pin, say that an abort after authorisation spends the look, and fix the re-pin procedure. One residual risk if the pins file is written with the present guard: the only mechanical barrier to a look is then a file named FREEZE in a workstream-writable directory, which is why holding the pins file until the guard is fixed is the safer order. It costs only a short delay to pool fits and matches §8.2 L785-786 as written.

lead_points.point: (4) / (b) the 97 unscored ADORE test partitions: stay or leave
lead_points.ruling: The rows of the 97 unscored ADORE challenge x split test partitions stay in the T1/T6 universe (4,632 rows: 3,176 train_pool, 1,456 T1_test, 0 T6a_test, 0 T6b_test). No workstream scores any of the 97 partitions, and no model fitted on train_pool is scored on any ADORE partition, before all three looks are complete. After the looks an ADORE partition may be scored only with a lead ruling, with every result_id of T1_test, T6a_test and T6b_test removed from its test rows first (those ids are spent under rule 1) and the removed count reported. At each look the scored-partition set derived from the registry must still equal the eight partitions behind the frozen spent-id list, or the look does not proceed.
lead_points.reason: Verified by keys: 105 test partitions, 8 scored (12 registry spellings), 97 unscored; the scored union is 28,265 ids, set-equal to the frozen list, and 0 of them are in any split role. 'Leave' is the strictest reading on row-independence and would not lower a bar (it removes 12.8 % of T1_test and raises its MDE). I still recommend 'stay': no held-out score has been read on these rows, so rule 1 does not make them spent and there is no leak to remove; no M4 protocol reserves any of the 97; and leaving forces a third rebuild (_v3) of a label-blind artefact after its power table has been read, with every count and gate changing. The freeze sentence gives the protection that matters (no ADORE look can spend T1 rows first, and T1's rows are never re-used for a second claim) and only adds restrictions. lead_points.point: (f) descriptive-by-default, and the path to an honest powered claim
lead_points.ruling: Under L4 none of T1_test, T6a_test or T6b_test as constituted (micro-RMSE, governing MDE 0.0959 / 0.1027 / 0.1033 at icc 0.5; 0.1911 / 0.2047 / 0.2044 at icc 1.0) can carry a §15.1 label: all three are descriptive only. The words 'by default' and every sentence making a label available 'if the realised difference exceeds the governing MDE' (L87-90, L657-660, §12.1 as a route to a label, §15.3) are struck. Conditions (a)-(j) are still computed and reported in full as the pre-registered descriptive reading; a result that would have met all of them is reported as 'exceeds the pre-registered MDE on an under-powered block; no SOTA label', and a result that does not is a measured null. A label on these questions needs a new, separately stamped track (lead point f). Path: a powered confirmatory claim is sought on a NEW track with more data or a harder task (RESEARCH_PLAN §15.5; sota_campaign rule 1: future data, a new geography or a new source), opened only by its own amendment, reviewed and stamped before any pool fit, whose label-free governing MDE at icc 1.0 is at or below an effect size the workstream commits to in writing before that power table is computed. Options (i)-(iii) of §15.3 (lower icc, finer unit, tighter cut-off) are refused. The stats lens's unit-balanced estimand is not adopted by this stamp: it may be proposed only as such a separately stamped addendum, with micro-RMSE still reported with equal prominence and a point difference in the candidate's favour on micro-RMSE also required.
lead_points.reason: L4's text excludes a label on a block that cannot detect a realistic gain, and the amendment concedes that for all three. On the unit-balanced estimand: its icc 1.0 figures are consistent with the power file's own scaling (MDE x sqrt(effective n) = 1.025 in t1t6_mde_v2.json, so 1.025/sqrt(546) = 0.044, /sqrt(694) = 0.039, /sqrt(289) = 0.060 on full blocks); I did not verify the icc 0.5 figures, and the governing values on the in-domain and no-shared-reference strata would be higher. It is a change of estimand chosen after its effect on power was seen, it is neither more data nor a harder task, and even so its gate (about 0.04 to 0.06) sits inside the 0.029 to 0.070 range of effects this project has measured, so it would be borderline rather than clearly powered. The clean route is more hold-out units.
